title: Edge session fracture tolerance and proportional evacuation plan
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Objective: Implement an active-active edge failover pattern that minimizes user-visible session disruption and keeps token/stream continuity for hosted API customers during regional evacuations. This ticket scopes a pragmatic design and an executable plan: proportional traffic evacuation, stream-aware handoff, circuit-breaker tuning, and tiered load-shedding to satisfy SLOs (availability + latency) while bounding cost and cold-start risk.

Scope:
- Gateway/edge routing behavior for hosted API (edge proxies + session coordinators).
- Streaming/session continuity for long-lived connections (websocket/HTTP2 chunked streaming).
- Interaction with KV prefix cache and model-inference runtime (KV sync / cache warming).
- Circuit breaker thresholds and graceful load-shedding policies by customer tier.
- Observability, runbooks, and automated test harness for chaos/failover.

Out of scope: persistent storage replication across regions (handled by infra), dedicated capacity contracts changes, and private on-prem control plane.

Design highlights and decisions:
1) Proportional evacuation with SLO-aware weighting: when a region signals evacuation (maintenance, capacity pressure), traffic is drained from that region in proportional batches to target regions using a per-route SLO budget. Traffic shifts are rate-limited by per-route headroom and token-preservation constraints to avoid overloading target nodes and violating p95 latency SLO.
2) Stream-aware drain windows: long-lived streaming sessions receive a soft-handoff window (default 45s) where we attempt a seamless replay/continuation using client-side resume tokens + server-side KV checkpointing. If resume fails by timeout, fallback path preserves partial output and returns a deterministic error payload and retry suggestion.
3) KV sync & cache warming: before shifting >10% of traffic to a target pool, we pre-warm KV prefixes for active sessions using a bounded background sync (priority queue) and warm model variants where feasible. This reduces first-token latency on the receiving side.
4) Circuit breaker layering: three-tier CBs (instance-level, pool-level, region-level) with dynamic thresholds derived from current SLO headroom. If pool-level CB trips, traffic is proportionally diverted to remaining healthy pools; if region-level CB trips, we trigger full-region evacuation playbook. CB thresholds are tied to error-rate, p99 latency, and queued-inflight tokens.
5) Priority-based load-shedding: implement soft and hard shedding buckets per customer tier. Soft shedding returns degradations (shorter max tokens, reduced sampling) for P3/P2; hard shedding returns short 429/503 for best-effort customers when headroom exhausted.
6) Regression safety: rollouts gated by synthetic session-based smoke tests and a targeted canary that simulates 1k concurrent streaming sessions and verifies continuity and latency.

Telemetry & SLO mapping:
- Primary SLOs: availability (successful end-to-end request completion) and latency p95/p99 for completed requests.
- Evacuation-specific metrics: drain_progress_pct, kv_prewarm_latency, resume_success_rate, session_loss_pct, spillover_error_rate.
- Error budget actions: automated slowdown of rollouts and activation of stricter shedding rules when error budget <10% for route.

Operational playbook (high level):
- Detection: automated alarms when region-level health < target (SLO headroom trigger) or manual operator trigger.
- Pre-flight: quorum checks, prewarm KV/model, calculate proportional split plan.
- Execute: incrementally reroute batches using traffic controller with telemetry validation after each step.
- Verify: smoke tests + telemetry checks verify that p95 remains within target. If failure, revert using stored traffic plan.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: resumed streams diverge in model state (context/kvs). Mitigation: limit resume to stateless prompts where possible; surface clear retry semantics to applications.
- Risk: prewarming increases transient cost. Mitigation: prewarm only active prefixes and cap parallelism.
- Risk: cascading CBs cause oscillation. Mitigation: add cooldown windows and use stateful counters with jittered backoffs.

Deliverables: design doc, control-plane changes (traffic controller), edge proxy drain implementation, KV prewarm worker, circuit-breaker control hooks, observability dashboards, runbook, automated tests.

Estimate breakdown (13 points): design spike (2), control-plane changes (4), edge proxy + streaming handoff (3), KV prewarm worker (2), dashboards & tests (2).
acceptance_criteria: Automated chaos test: simulated region evacuation causes <=2% lost sessions for priority customers in a 1k-stream synthetic workload
Resume success rate >= 95% for resumable streaming sessions under controlled failover conditions
Drain progress metric shows proportional traffic shift matching planned weights within +/-5% during rollout
Canary run (1k concurrent simulated sessions) maintains p95 latency within SLO; if not, rollout auto-aborts and reverts
Circuit breaker trips propagate correctly: instance -> pool -> region with documented cooldown behavior
Dashboards for drain_progress_pct, resume_success_rate, kv_prewarm_latency, and session_loss_pct created and linked in attachments
Runbook with step-by-step operator commands checked into runbooks repo and referenced from ticket
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Malik: Kickoff spike completed. Validated that existing traffic controller supports per-route proportional weighting but lacks stream-aware drain hooks. Spoke with runtime team about KV checkpoint API gaps.

2026-03-11 - Connor Hayes: Implemented a prototype for drain controller that streams planned weights and supports pause/resume. Found race where prewarm worker floods target pool if parallelism unconstrained — added backpressure plan.

2026-03-12 - Design review: PM and SRE feedback: increase soft-handoff default to 45s and add explicit client retry headers for resumable sessions. Action: update API contract and SDK docs to include resume token semantics.
2026-03-13 - Connor Hayes: Opened PR with control-plane changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/447 (waiting for eng review).
2026-03-14 - QA: wrote synthetic streaming test harness and found resume_success_rate only 82% in emulated high-latency path. Follow-up: tighten KV checkpoint frequency and cap prewarm concurrency.
notes: Follow-up tasks: add feature-flag gated runtime resume protocol; coordinate with SDK teams for client-visible resume header (X-Redwood-Resume).
Consider a temporary compatibility fallback to stateless model variants for customers with strict uptime requirements.
Plan staged rollout: dev -> staging (5% traffic) -> canary (10% of production routes) -> full gradual rollout with telemetry gates.
